paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CCE-C1 — Chapter 1: Chinese Communist Intelligence Organizations (Peter Mattis & Matthew Brazil, 2019)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In the opening chapter of *Chinese Communist Espionage: An Intelligence Primer* (Naval Institute Press, 2019, Ebook pp. 32–63, 18 PDF pages, 163 endnote callouts), intelligence specialists Peter Mattis and Dr. Matthew Brazil construct the most comprehensive open-source organizational history of Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and PRC civilian and military intelligence agencies from 1921 to 2018. Challenging Beijing's official 'hidden battlefront' (`隐蔽战线`) propaganda—which portrays an unbroken, heroic lineage—the authors demonstrate that CCP intelligence organs repeatedly fractured under ideological purges and reorganized to meet shifting domestic and foreign threats.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Revolutionary Predecessors (1927–1949, pp. 1–6)**: Traces the **1927 Wuhan Special Operations Branch** (`特务工作处`), the **1927–35 Shanghai Special Services Section (`中央特科`, *Teke*)** (nearly wiped out by **Gu Shunzhang's April 1931 defection**, saved by **Li Kenong and Qian Zhuangfei**), the **1931–39 Political Protection Bureau (`国家政治保卫局`, PPB)** (warned of the Fifth Encirclement by **Mo Xiong** in Oct 1934), and the **1939–49 Social Affairs Department (`中共中央社会部`, SAD)** under **Kang Sheng** and **Li Kenong** (operating >5,000 agents in SW China including **Yan Baohang** and **Ji Chaoding**, before Kang's 1943 *Salvation* purge was halted by **Dimitrov's Dec 1943 telegram**).
• **MPS, Interim Bodies & the Central Investigation Department (1949–1983, pp. 6–14)**: Covers the **Ministry of Public Security (`公安部`, MPS)** under **Luo Ruiqing, Xie Fuzhi, Li Zhen, and Hua Guofeng** (700,000 executed in 1950–51; *hukou* and neighborhood surveillance; Sept 1958 expulsion of Soviet advisers; Cultural Revolution reduction of MPS HQ to 126 staff; July 1983 transfer of counterespionage to the MSS; and the June 1999 **610 Office**), the 1949–55 military/party interim bodies, and the **1955–83 Central Investigation Department (`中央调查部`, CID / 'Organ in the Western Garden')**—born amid the **April 1955 Pan Hannian purge (800–1,000 intelligence cadres purged)** and abolished in 1983 after CID chief **Luo Qingchang** defied **Deng Xiaoping's July 7, 1979 speech** against using diplomatic cover.
• **Military Intelligence (`2PLA` -> `JSD-IB`) & the Ministry of State Security (`国家安全部`, MSS) (pp. 14–18)**: Maps **2PLA's** 6–7 bureaus, **CIISS** and **CFISS**, the **Nov 26, 2015** reorganization into the **JSD Intelligence Bureau** and **Strategic Support Force (SSF)**, and the **MSS's** four-wave expansion, **Central State Security Commission (CSSC)** oversight, and **18 numbered headquarters bureaus**.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Core Organizational & Doctrinal Terms**: 'Hidden Battlefront' (`隐蔽战线`, *Yinbi zhanxian*); 'One Organization, Two Nameplates' (`一个机构两块牌子`, SAD & Central Intelligence Dept, 1941–49); 'Organ in the Western Garden' (`中直西苑机关`, CID); 'Sensitive Units' (`敏感单位`, *min'gan danwei*); 'Secret Line' (1st Bureau) vs. 'Open Line' (2nd Bureau).
• **Key Quantitative Benchmarks**: Long March attrition: `86,000` (Oct 1934) -> `20,000` (May 1935) -> `5,000` (Oct 1935); Dutton's 'Three 90% Problems' (`770,000` new CCP members, 1937–40); 1950 MPS spy cases broken: `2,070`; 1950–51 Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries: `700,000` executions; 1955 *Sufan* campaign: `>18 million` investigated, `257,551` purged (`800–1,000` intelligence cadres purged with Pan Hannian); 1968 MPS HQ staff: reduced to `126` (`1/10` strength); Crime rate spike: `24 per 100,000` (1969) -> `60 per 100,000` (1973); 1982 Soviet spy arrests: `200` Chinese citizens; MSS Headquarters: `18` numbered bureaus.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
All 4 reference rows (`CCEC1-R01` to `CCEC1-R04`) are rated `ok` (noting minor Chinese character/pinyin slips on pp. 2 and 5: `'特务特务工作处'`, `'Zhongyang junwei teke'` for `中央特科`, and `'政风'` for `整风`). Within our 90-document dashboard, `CCE-C1` provides the essential intelligence-community counterpart to our PLA/PLAN organizational studies in Batch 3 (`CMR-56`, `CMR-57`, `CMR-58`) and Batch 7 (`CNN-00` to `CNN-07`).

paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CCE-C6 — Chapter 6: Espionage during China's Rise (Peter Mattis & Matthew Brazil, 2019)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In Chapter 6 of *Chinese Communist Espionage: An Intelligence Primer* (Naval Institute Press, 2019, Ebook pp. 211–230, 12 PDF pages, 60 endnote callouts), Peter Mattis and Matthew Brazil audit **34 post-1989 espionage cases and intelligence units**. They demonstrate that China's intelligence services have achieved 'world-class status' by fusing **cyber network exploitation** (PLA Unit 61398 and MSS hacks of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management and Taiwanese residential databases) with **traditional human intelligence (HUMINT)**—using co-optees/cut-outs, think-tank and academic exchange covers, third-country resort meetings, financial/business inducements, and family leverage to acquire national defense secrets and Five-Year Plan dual-use technologies.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Cyber-HUMINT Integration & Regional MSS Powerhouses (`JSSD` & `SSSB`, pp. 1–2, 7, 10)**: Details how the **Jiangsu State Security Department (JSSD)** combined corporate insiders, hackers, and NUAA researchers to steal commercial turbofan engine technology (leading to the 2018 Belgium arrest and extradition of JSSD deputy division director **Xu Yanjun**), and how the **Shanghai State Security Bureau (SSSB)** uses the **Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences (SASS)** and throwaway consulting firms to pitch U.S., Japanese, and Taiwanese targets.
• **U.S. & European Espionage Cases (pp. 2–11)**: Profiles **Gregg Bergersen, James Fondren, and Kuo Tai-shen** (2008–09); **Katrina Leung and FBI Agent J. J. Smith** (2003); **Chi Mak and Tai Mak** (2007–08); **Glenn Duffie Shriver** (2010); **Lt. Col. Benjamin Bishop and Claudia He** (2014); **Kun Shan Chun** (2017); **Candice Claiborne** (2017); **Jerry Chun Shing Lee** (2018); **Kevin Mallory** (2018); **Ron Rockwell Hansen** (2018); **Paul Doumitt** (1988); **Helen Gao** (2010); **Nate Thayer** (2014); and Uighur/Tibetan diaspora spies **Baibur Maihesuti** (2010) and **Dorjee Gyantsan** (2018).
• **Taiwanese Military & Intelligence Penetration (pp. 3–12)**: Profiles 17 cases where 2PLA, MSS/SSSB, and United Front officers used retired Taiwanese officers as cut-outs and Southeast Asian/Australian travel to recruit active-duty generals and colonels—including **double agent Li Zhihao** (traded in Nov 2015 for kidnapped MIB officers Chu Kung-hsun and Hsu Chang-kuo), **Brig. Gen. Lo Hsien-che** (Army electronic info chief), **Lt. Col. Yuan Hsiao-feng** (12 life sentences), **Maj. Gen. Hsieh Chia-kang** (missile defense command), and **Zhen Xiaojiang's** air force spy ring.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Operational Tradecraft Concepts**: Cyber-HUMINT integration (OPM & Taiwan database hacks enabling target spotting); Co-optees / Cut-outs (civilian collaborators operating under business, academic, or journalistic covers); Third-Country Resort Recruitment (Bali, Cebu, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Australia, France/Italy, Belgium); Family Leverage (supporting Candice Claiborne's son in Shanghai; caring for Tai Mak's mother-in-law).
• **Case Metrics**: `34` alphabetical case/unit entries (`17` Taiwan-related, `14` U.S.-related, `3` Europe/Japan-related); Katrina Leung FBI payments: `$1.7 million` (1982–2000); Ron Hansen MSS offer: `$300,000/yr` (`~$200,000` paid via Visa merchant account); Yuan Hsiao-feng 2PLA payments: `~$269,000` (`12` life sentences); Lo Hsien-che 2PLA payments: `$100,000–$200,000` per delivery; Jerry Lee MSS pitch: `$100,000` + life care; Glenn Shriver SSSB payment: `$70,000`; German MP LinkedIn pitch: `€30,000`; Kevin Mallory SSSB payment: `$25,000` for `8` classified documents.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
Of the 4 reference rows audited in `CCE-C6`, 3 are rated `ok` and **1 is rated `fix` (`[CCEC6-R02]`)**:
• **`[CCEC6-R02]` (`fix` — Misidentifying Male CNNC Nuclear Chief Kang Rixin [`康日新`] as Kuo Tai-shen's 'Mistress' on p. 7 & Calling USAF Lt. Col. James Fondren `'Col. James Fondren, USA (Ret.)'` on p. 5)**: On p. 7, the authors write that Kuo Tai-shen and his handler *'used Kuo's mistress, Kang Rixin, as an intermediary and met in her Beijing apartment'*—confusing Kuo's female intermediary with **Kang Rixin (`康日新`)**, the male General Manager of China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) purged in 2009! Additionally, p. 5 labels James Fondren a retired U.S. Army Colonel (`'Col. James Fondren, USA (Ret.)'`), contradicting p. 7 (`'a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel'`).

paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CCE-C7 — Chapter 7: Intelligence and Surveillance in China, Then and Now (Peter Mattis & Matthew Brazil, 2019)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In the concluding chapter of *Chinese Communist Espionage: An Intelligence Primer* (Naval Institute Press, 2019, Ebook pp. 231–241, 6 PDF pages, 30 endnote callouts), Peter Mattis and Matthew Brazil connect the 90-year historical evolution of CCP intelligence (1927–present) with the modern domestic surveillance state inside the PRC. They argue that Beijing governs through a two-tier system: a universal administrative **'baseline of surveillance'** (`身份证` ID cards, `户口` *hukou*, `档案` *dang'an*, hotel/PSB foreigner registration, and **Alibaba's *Zhima* Credit**) that flags anomalies, backed by **six warrantless MPS/MSS intensive surveillance methods** that dominate any target area like *'the U.S. Navy on the high seas.'*

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Chinese Intelligence, 1927–Present (pp. 1–3)**: Reviews the **1929–30 'Three Heroes of the Dragon's Lair'** (Li Kenong's trio, taught to MSS trainees like Brécourt Manor at West Point), **Gu Shunzhang's April 1931 defection**, **Mo Xiong's Oct 1934 warning**, **Kang Sheng's Yan'an spy hunt**, and the **three great exoduses of PRC foreign intelligence officers** in **1955** (Pan Hannian + 800–1,000 purged), **1966–67** (Cultural Revolution PLA takeover of the CID), and **1983** (Deng forcing out Luo Qingchang when the MSS replaced the CID).
• **Surveillance in China Today (pp. 3–6)**: Contrasts routine PSB 'accountability' tracking of PRC citizens and **~600,000 resident foreigners** with targeted scrutiny of Tibetans, Uighurs, dissidents, and foreigners in **'sensitive units' (`敏感的单位`)**. Profiles **Alibaba / Ant Financial's *Zhima* (Sesame) Credit** (6M court defaulters, **2,094 CCP members**, 2012 **Group Party Committee**, and 20-year MPS veteran **Shao Xiaofeng** as Chief Risk Officer), details the **six basic MPS/MSS intensive surveillance efforts** (foot/vehicle, urban CCTV, phone recording/tracking, email/online monitoring, contact interviews, credit card/ATM data), and highlights the **2014/2016 antispy campaign**.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Surveillance & Intelligence Concepts**: 'Three Heroes of the Dragon's Lair' (`龙潭三杰`); 'Baseline of Surveillance' (`身份证` *shenfen zheng* + `户口` *hukou* + `档案` *dang'an*); 'Sensitive Units' (`敏感的单位`, *min gan de danwei*); 'Social Credit System' (`社会信用体系`, *shehui xinyong tixi*) & *Zhima* Credit (`芝麻信用`); State Administration for Religious Affairs (`国家宗教事务局`).
• **Key Quantitative Benchmarks**: Three intelligence exoduses: `1955` (`800–1,000` purged), `1966–67`, and `1983`; Resident foreigners in China: `~600,000` (plus tens of thousands of monthly tourists); Court-fine defaulters integrated into *Zhima* Credit: `6 million`; CCP members employed at Alibaba: `2,094` (Group Party Committee formed `2012`); Intensive MPS/MSS surveillance methods: `6` core techniques; Antispy campaign: begun secretly in `early 2014`, publicized in `2016`.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance

paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CN21-C1 — Chapter One: China's Maritime Power Ambition (Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt, 2020)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In Chapter One of *China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power: Theory, Practice, and Implications* (Naval Institute Press, 2020, Ebook pp. 17–34, 10 PDF pages, 58 endnote callouts), Rear Admiral Michael A. McDevitt, USN (Ret.) traces how China—for millennia a continental power—elevated becoming a **'maritime great power' (`海洋强国`, *haiyang qiangguo*)** and building a **'world-class military' (by 2035/2049)** into core national strategy under Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. McDevitt shows that this maritime turn is driven by four strategic imperatives articulated by Xi in July 2013: defending China's eastern economic heartland from seaborne attack, alleviating acute **'SLOC anxiety'** over seaborne trade/oil/food lifelines, protecting expanding **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** assets and citizens abroad, and compelling the reunification of **Taiwan** to breach the First Island Chain.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **From *Haiyang Qiangguo* (2012) to 'World-Class Forces' (2017, pp. 1–4)**: Tracks Hu Jintao's 2012 18th Party Congress report, the 2012 Defense White Paper (Apr 2013), and Xi Jinping's 2017 19th Party Congress deadlines (**2035 basic modernization; 2049/2050 world-class forces**). Defines Chinese 'maritime power' (strong navy + coast guard + maritime militia + merchant marine + shipbuilding + fisheries) and critiques Beijing's use of domestic law to enforce its 'maritime rights and interests' (9DL) over UNCLOS.
• **Exploring China's Four Strategic Ends (pp. 4–10)**: (1) *Homeland Defense*: Quotes the **2013 AMS *Science of Military Strategy*** that China's main security threat comes from the sea, recalling the 1840 Opium War and Century of Humiliation; (2) *Trade, 'SLOC Anxiety' & 'Blue Granary'*: Documents China's rise from 100th in world trade (1978) to #1 exporter (2009) and #1 trader (2013), **#1 crude oil importer in late 2017 (8.4M bpd, 85% by tanker)**, **80–90% seaborne trade share**, the Dec 2008 Gulf of Aden deployment (after 111 pirate attacks / 42 hijackings in 2008), and the 12th Five-Year Plan's 'ocean economy' and **~2,700-ship distant-water fishing fleet**; (3) *Taiwan & the First Island Chain*: Quotes the **2005 *Science of Military Strategy*** on Taiwan's geostrategic centrality to breaking out of the First Island Chain and reviews the 1996 crisis that spurred A2/AD; and (4) *Maritime Silk Road & Overseas Citizens*: Links Xi's Oct 2013 BRI announcement to the **Djibouti base (2017)** and the **2011 Libya / 2015 Yemen evacuations**.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Strategic Concepts**: 'Maritime Great Power' (`海洋强国`, *haiyang qiangguo*); 'World-Class Forces' (`世界一流军队`, 2035 / 2049 timetable); 'SLOC Anxiety'; 'Blue Economy' & 'Blue Granary' (`蓝色粮仓`); 'Main Strategic Direction' (Taiwan, since 1993); 'First Island Chain' containment.
• **Key Quantitative Benchmarks**: China world trade rank: `#100` (1978) -> `#1` exporter (2009) & `#1` trader (2013); Seaborne share of China's trade: `80–90%`; Crude oil imports (late 2017): `8.4 million bpd` (`#1` globally, `~85%` by tanker); 2008 Somali piracy: `111` attacks, `42` hijackings; Distant-water fishing fleet: `~2,700` vessels.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
Of the 4 reference rows audited in `CN21-C1`, 3 are rated `ok` and **1 is rated `fix` (`[CN21C1-R01]`)**:

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In Chapter Two of *China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power* (Naval Institute Press, 2020, Ebook pp. 35–55, 13 PDF pages, 56 endnote callouts, Tables 1 & 2), Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt traces the 45-year operational learning curve (1975–2020) that transformed the PLA Navy from a coastal force dismissed by Western officers in the late 1980s as a 'junkyard navy' into a professional expeditionary force. McDevitt demonstrates that over twelve years of continuous **Gulf of Aden antipiracy deployments (2008–2020)** served as a real-world **'blue-water operations laboratory'**—teaching the PLAN underway replenishment, commercial port logistics via **COSCO**, overseas basing (**Djibouti**), 24/7 global command and control, overseas engine repair, naval diplomacy, and citizen evacuations while giving **~27,000 officers and sailors** distant-seas experience.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Early Voyages Abroad (1980–2008, Tables 1 & 2, pp. 1–6)**: Covers the **May 1980 18-ship South Pacific DF-5 ICBM recovery mission** (4,300 nm), **Table 1 (`1985–1999`: 7 overseas voyages)**, **Table 2 (`2000–2008`: 16 deployments, including the 2002 123-day, 32,000-nm global circumnavigation by *Qingdao* & *Taicang*)**, and the **2007 watershed exercises** (*Aman 07*, WPNS, and *Guangzhou*'s 87-day European voyage exercising with carrier *Ark Royal*).
• **Antipiracy Patrols as a Blue-Water Laboratory (2008–2020, pp. 6–13)**: Tracks **33 rotations (58 warships deployed: 43 Type 054/054A FFGs, 15 DDGs, 3 Type 071 LPDs)**, SHADE coordination with India/Japan/South Korea (2012), the expansion of replenishment ships from **2 overworked *Fuchi* AOEs (*Qiandaohu* making 13 deployments in 6 years) to 11 modern ships (9 *Fuchi* + 2 Type 901)**, port calls at **Salalah** and the **Aug 1, 2017 opening of the Djibouti base**, cutting local supply purchase time with **COSCO from >20 days (5 entities) to 2 days**, the **24/7 Beijing 'two-level flat command link,'** the **May 2010 Djibouti gas-turbine engine replacement**, ~210-day deployments (100,000–120,000 nm), the **2011 Libya and 2015 Yemen evacuations**, and **~27,000 personnel** trained by April 2019.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In Chapter 5 of *China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power* (Naval Institute Press, 2020, Ebook pp. 110–124, 9 PDF pages, 44 endnotes), Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt examines the **anti-access (A2)** phase of a PLA counterintervention campaign in the Philippine Sea. Updating his classic 2007 chapter (*'Sea Denial with Chinese Characteristics'*, `CFNSF-04`), McDevitt disaggregates the PLA's ocean surveillance system and its **'troika' of A2 strike forces** (land-based missile bombers/fighters, attack submarines, and anti-ship ballistic missiles), concluding that while the DF-21D/DF-26 ASBM kill chain is vulnerable to electronic jamming and decoys, the combination of ASBMs, ~45 hunting submarines, and multi-regiment H-6K/JH-7 raids poses the gravest sea-control challenge the U.S. Navy has faced since 1945—tempered by the PLA's institutional difficulty in achieving seamless four-service jointness.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Surveillance: The Prerequisite for Counterintervention (pp. 1–3)**: Maps the land-based OTH radar, air-breathing UAV (**CH-5**), and space-based ISR architecture (**~134 remote-sensing satellites across 28 types**, led by SAR wake-imaging satellites and the **60-to-138 satellite *Jilin-1* optical/video constellation**, backed by #1 world space launch totals in 2018 [39] and 2019 [32]) covering 32M sq miles out to 2,000 nm.
• **The Airpower Leg (pp. 3–5, Map 3)**: Audits the **90 H-6K bombers** (1,350-nm radius, carrying 6 supersonic **YJ-12 ASCMs** = **108 ASCMs per 18-plane raid**; 7 total H-6G/K maritime regiments), **3 Il-78 tankers** and **Y-20 tanker** conversions for Su-30 fighter escorts through the 130-nm Miyako Strait, **24 Su-30MK2s**, and **260 JH-7/7As** (140 PLAAF + 120 PLANAF).
• **The Submarine Leg (pp. 5–6, 9)**: Details the 70–78 boat force (~45 available for warship hunting; **64% ASCM-capable** with SS-N-27 *Sizzler* and 290-nm **YJ-18** plus wake-homing under-keel torpedoes; 14–18 day *Yuan* AIP endurance) and **Lyle Goldstein's** discovery of the **430,000-sq-ft Huludao assembly hall** able to build **4 SSNs simultaneously**.
• **The ASBM Leg (`DF-21D` & `DF-26`, pp. 7–9)**: Examines the 100-km (53-nm) MaRV terminal guidance envelope, **Adm. Philip Davidson's disclosure of the July 2019 6-missile DF-21D test salvo in the South China Sea**, kill-chain vulnerabilities, and the post-1986 Goldwater-Nichols lesson that true jointness across the PLAN, PLAAF, PLARF, and SSF takes decades.

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: In the concluding chapter (Chapter 8, Ebook pp. 172–188, 9 PDF pages, 35 endnotes) of *China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power* (Naval Institute Press, 2020), Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt synthesizes China's comprehensive maritime power, evaluates the PLA's institutional and human readiness, and projects the size of the PLA Navy in **2035**. McDevitt argues that China is already a great maritime power by every tangible metric (#1 in shipbuilding, fishing, coast guard cutters, merchant ship count, and total naval hulls), that by 2035 the PLAN will field approximately **425 warships (265 blue-water + 160 near-seas)**, and that while the U.S. Navy retains five qualitative 'aces' (nuclear submarines, nuclear carrier air wings, 90+ Aegis warships, unmanned/directed-energy tech, and combat-seasoned crews), any future U.S. president in a conflict with China will face a contested sea-control fight last experienced by Franklin Roosevelt in 1941.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Grand Strategy & Addressing SLOC Anxiety (pp. 1–4)**: Links the 1999 'going out' strategy and BRI to protecting >30 SLOCs connecting >1,200 ports in 150 countries, highlights Adm. Liu Huaqing's Dec 1941 *Prince of Wales* / *Repulse* lesson on the fatal vulnerability of surface ships without air cover, and quotes the 2019 DoD report on CSSC/CSIC shipbuilding self-sufficiency.
• **China Is a Great Maritime Power Today (pp. 4–5)**: Compares fish catch (16.3M vs. 5.2M tons US), coast guard cutters >500t (225 CCG vs. 40 USCG), and state-owned merchant fleets (5,552 Chinese ships [183M DWT] vs. Greece 4,371 [330M DWT], Japan 3,841, and U.S. 2,073; carrying 25% of Chinese trade and integrating defense-spec Ro-Ro ferries into PLA exercises).
• **How Good Is the PLA Navy? (pp. 5–7)**: Reviews the 2015–16 reorganization (5 Joint Theater Commands, CMC centralization), Dr. David Finkelstein's institutional critique, Dennis Blasko on **'peace disease' (`和平病`)**, and **Xi Jinping's 'Five Cannots' (`五个不会`)**.
• **How Large Will the PLAN Be in 2035? (`425` Ships) & Concluding Thoughts (pp. 7–9)**: Forecasts **265 blue-water warships** (including **5–6 carriers** and **~1.5 SSNs/yr** from Huludao) + **160 near-seas ships** = **425 warships by 2035**, weighed against the U.S. Navy's 355-ship goal and five qualitative 'aces.'

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Comprehensive Maritime Power Indicators (pp. 4–5)**: 2013 fish catch: China `16.3M tons` vs. U.S. `5.2M tons`; Coast Guard cutters (`>500t`): CCG `225` vs. USCG `40`; State-owned merchant fleet (Jan 2018): `#1` China `5,552` ships (`183M DWT`, `#3` in DWT), `#2` Greece `4,371` (`>330M DWT`, `#1` in DWT), `#3` Japan `3,841`, `#6` U.S. `2,073` (Chinese ships carry `25%` of PRC trade); 2020 naval ship count: PLAN `~300` vs. USN `~264`.
